newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo Wellcome sets out R&D pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome sets out R&D pipeline.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Friday that ten new drug molecules had entered development in the first four months of 1997 and that it expected to have more than 20 in development by the end of the year.

In a detailed research and development update to be presented to analysts later on Friday, Glaxo Wellcome deputy chairman and chief executive Sir Richard Sykes said the company was on track to meet its prediction of double-digit sales growth in 1999.
"The quality, depth and diversity of our pipeline supports our view that Glaxo Wellcome is without equal in its commitment to finding new medicines through leading- edge science," said Sykes.

James Niedel, research and development director, said the company was "on track to fulfil our stated objective of bringing three significant new medicines per annum to the market from the year 2000 onwards."

Glaxo Wellcome faces the challenge of making up for an expected plunge in sales of its blockbuster anti-ulcer drug Zantac when its key U.S. patent expires in July. It will present the details of its development portfolio to analysts in London from 0730 GMT, and in New York on Monday.
Glaxo Wellcome said that its respiratory business, which had sales of 1.8 billion stg last year, had overtaken its gastro-intestinal drugs, including Zantac, as its biggest therapeutic sector.

Among products highlighted in the update were Romozin, a treatment for type II diabetes, Lamivudine for treating Hepatitis B, Seretide for asthma, antibiotics Grepafloxacin and Sanfetrinem, Naramig for migraine and Zyban for smoking cessation. The company also said it had two new drugs for the treatment of HIV and AIDS in development.
Niedel said that currently in the drugs industry only 10 compounds out of 100 entering development actually reached the market, and of these only three recovered their costs.
"To improve this situation improvements have to be made in target selection, drug candidate selection and product development."
Niedel added that "our excellence in all aspects of R&D gives us confidence that we will achieve the performance goals we have set."
